planned_work.acceptance_criteria: Use a pinned, inspected official OpenClaw channel plugin SDK revision and a real example plugin; document actual package exports, entrypoints, lifecycle hooks and version compatibility, without inventing an API. | Specify mapping of Tavi server origin, Tavi account ID, peer/group conversation IDs, signed-in session and inbound/outbound OpenClaw message envelopes; distinguish platform identity from display names. | Specify reliable wake/catch-up, cursor/idempotency and authenticated replay behavior, shutdown/restart cleanup and bounded history. planned_work.title: OpenClaw native channel for ordinary Tavi messaging
planned_work.acceptance_criteria: Install and enable the native Tavi channel through OpenClaw plugin management; connect one dedicated ordinary Tavi account with private credentials and no privileged Social or LoopRD service token. | Human -> Tavi DM -> OpenClaw agent -> Tavi reply works with independent per-peer session routing and sender display-name metadata; outgoing messages are sent by the authenticated agent account. | Contact invitations and game.challenge.requested/response events reach the right agent account as typed events; manual acceptance and opt-in peer/game allowlisted automatic acceptance use the normal Social APIs, with no game seat grants. | Groups are supported only when Tavi group APIs and ACLs actually exist; unsupported group capabilities are advertised as unavailable rather than simulated. | Channel starts/stops/reconnects with OpenClaw, uses replay-safe bounded reconciliation and does not require tavi-openclaw-service.mjs to run.

planned_work.title: Native Tavi channel security, migration and live acceptance
planned_work.acceptance_criteria: Using two human Tavi accounts and one separately authenticated OpenClaw account, demonstrate DM both directions and a challenged game acceptance entirely through native OpenClaw channel (external watcher disabled). | Verify authorization for accepted/unaccepted contacts, per-account isolation, event recipient scoping, allowlist enforcement, malicious inbound message containment and no credential in logs, prompts or outbound game URLs. | Stop/restart OpenClaw and disable network during pending messages/challenges; verify bounded catch-up, no unrecoverable loss within server retention, no runaway duplicate sends and explicit limitation documentation. | Confirm native plugin installation/upgrades and downgrade/rollback; only then propose disabling external watcher, without deleting CLI support or changing ordinary Tavi clients. | Operator reviews actual OpenClaw Gateway runtime traces, Tavi inbox messages, Windows UI and server-side authorization logs before marking Done.

planned_work.title: Life authoritative match creation and OpenClaw turn adapter
planned_work.acceptance_criteria: Life provides reviewed authenticated create/join/resume, inspect, legal_actions, act and end_turn endpoints with durable match IDs, validated Tavi subject-to-seat bindings and idempotent command IDs. | An accepted Tavi challenge is correlated to one operator-approved Life match; rejection/expiry/replay creates no seat and no game action, and match admission always requires Life authorization. | OpenClaw uses a game-specific legal-action adapter via independent Tavi identity and Life API; cannot act for another player, invent moves or bypass legal-action validation. | Two participants can disconnect, resume and complete legal Life turns; changes to match seats and closed state trigger accurate Social roster and notification updates. | Game backend changes are tracked and approved in the Life project workboard; this Tavi item records the dependency and integration evidence, not a claim of Life implementation.

planned_work.title: End-to-end Tavi, Atrium and Life multiplayer acceptance
planned_work.acceptance_criteria: Windows Tavi shows Life, user chooses Challenge against OpenClaw, native channel receives and accepts the invitation, and Life creates a verified playable match whose ID can be launched/resumed via Atrium. | Human plays legal turns versus OpenClaw, OpenClaw observes its own authorized seat and plays via Life game API, and the game progresses to a final state without a continuously connected host. | Open same match from another device after app/agent/backend restart; match and turns persist and all clients agree on the authoritative game state. | Verify two human players can also create/join/complete a game and private match conversation ACLs follow actual Life roster removal and closure. | Attempt replay, unauthorized seat access, expired invitations and stale/duplicate actions; all fail safely with no credential leakage. Obtain explicit operator sign-off.
